records.question: Is construction allowed here?
records.zones_text: planning zone O; in Zone O (Yamuna floodplain)
records.answer:
Active floodplain, which includes Zone O as a Yamuna floodplain, is designated a ‘no construction zone’ where only recreational uses are permitted, and all unauthorised construction must be demolished [C2].
The Delhi High Court has directed the removal of all encroachments and illegal construction on the Yamuna river bank and floodplain, reinforcing that such construction is not allowed [C3].

citations.doc_title: Master Plan for Delhi 2047 gazette notification (English)
Delhi High Court order on Yamuna floodplain encroachments (8 Jul 2024)

verdicts.reason: Clause ii states active floodplain is a ‘no construction zone’ with only recreational uses and demolition of unauthorised construction, but does not mention Zone O as a Yamuna floodplain.
Clause 6 orders removal of encroachments on the Yamuna river bank, river bed and drains, but does not explicitly mention the floodplain.

records.question: What are the rules for the active floodplain?
records.zones_text: planning zone O; in Zone O (Yamuna floodplain)
records.answer:
Active floodplain is designated as a ‘no construction zone’ where only recreational uses are permitted and all unauthorised construction, including religious structures, must be demolished by the concerned agency on priority [C1].
The zone is also described as a prohibited activity zone because encroachment diverts water and leads to floods, as acknowledged by respondents in the court proceedings [C5].

citations.doc_title: Master Plan for Delhi 2047 gazette notification (English)
Delhi High Court order on Yamuna floodplain encroachments (8 Jul 2024)

verdicts.reason: Clause ii states: "Active floodplain shall be a ‘no construction zone’ and only recreational uses shall be permitted. All unauthorised construction including religious structures shall be demolished by the concerned agency on priority."
Clause 3 says: "...the floodplain area is a prohibited activity zone... encroachment in this area leads to diversion of water leading to floods..."

records.question: Can I build a house here?
records.zones_text: planning zone L; in low density area
records.answer:
Low Density Area (LDA) comprises areas within the depth of one peripheral village revenue boundary along the border of NCTD and LDRA as defined in the Master Plan for Delhi 2047 [C2].
For residential use in LDA, the minimum plot size is 10,000 sq m and the development control norms are FAR 10, maximum ground coverage 15%, maximum building height 10 m, and a minimum rear‑of‑site (RoW) setback of 18 m [C1].

citations.doc_title: Master Plan for Delhi 2047 gazette notification (English)
Master Plan for Delhi 2047 gazette notification (English)

verdicts.reason: Clause 4.4 states LDA shall comprise areas within the depth of one peripheral village revenue boundary along the border of NCTD and LDRA.
Clause 4.4.3 lists Residential plot minimum 10,000 sq m with FAR 10, ground coverage max 15%, height max 10 m, min RoW 18 m.

records.question: Is construction allowed here?
records.zones_text: planning zone J; in Ridge / regional park
records.answer:
In the Ridge/Regional Park area, new construction is generally restricted and may be permitted only for socio‑cultural, recreational uses or essential government utilities and public infrastructure, subject to approval/NOC of the competent authority or statutory body [C1].
Any development within a Regional Park must comply with the specific controls set out for Regional Parks, including obtaining necessary approvals from the Forest Department and adhering to security and amenity provisions, and no general construction is allowed without such clearances [C3].

citations.doc_title: Master Plan for Delhi 2047 gazette notification (English)
Master Plan for Delhi 2047 gazette notification (English)

verdicts.reason: Clause ii and iii state that development is restricted to socio‑cultural, recreational uses, essential utilities and public infrastructure with approval/NOC

Clause ix(a) requires development to be in accordance with the Forest Department and (b) adds security provisions, but does not explicitly state that no general construction is allowed without such clearances

records.question: How much of my plot can I build on?
records.zones_text: planning zone G; in none of the six policy zones
records.answer:
For plotted housing the maximum ground coverage is 90% for plots up to 100 sqm and 75% for plots above 100 sqm up to 750 sqm, with the maximum FAR ranging from 350 for plots up to 250 sqm down to 200 for plots above 750 sqm as specified in clause 7.2.1 of the Master Plan (C6) [C6].
The minimum plot size for residential development is 32 sqm, and the total ground coverage and floor area for any plot category shall not be less than that available to the largest plot in the next lower category (C6) [C6].

citations.doc_title: Master Plan for Delhi 2047 gazette notification (English)

verdicts.reason: Clause lists 350 FAR only up to 100 sqm, then 300 up to 250 sqm, not 350 up to 250 sqm as sentence claims
Clause (ii) states minimum plot size 32 sqm and (iii) states ground coverage/floor area shall not be less than that of the largest plot in the next lower category
